messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Question
parts:
Hi there.

If you are behind a firewall or router and want to make it accessible from outside, you'll have to configure the firewall or router to do port forwarding of port 4949 to your own machine's IP address. You can run the linux command "ip addr" and find the "inet" field. If there are several, don't use the one that's 127.0.0.1.

Once you've done that (or you don't have a firewall/router) go to http://www.whatismyip.com or http://jsonip.com to see the IP address that your network presents to the outside world; that IP address should be the one you use from outside the network.

You might also have to allow port 4949 through on your software firewall--that is, the firewall software on your Linux box. If this is a fresh Ubuntu box then I highly recommend using the ufw package to manage your firewall; once ufw is installed and running I think it's just "ufw allow 4949", and maybe you have to do "ufw reload" after that. I think you can test if your software firewall will block requests by requesting http://ip-address-from-first-paragraph:4949, even from the same machine; if it succeeds, you're fine.

HTH,
-joe
